`TagDevice` now uses the inbound request `ctx`. If the client disconnects mid-auth (a common case for an anonymous browser session that redirects away), the context is cancelled and the DB write is aborted, but the request handler then continues and returns success. The device is therefore neither in the DB nor counted for future requests until it is seen again. The previous implementation used `context.Background()` with its own timeout precisely to avoid this. The new design should derive a detached context (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or a fresh background context) for the device-tag DB write so client cancellation doesn't drop the write.

Test name and assertions don't verify that the first device was actually counted

`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that the second `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. It does not assert on `CountDevices` before the second call to confirm the count actually reached the configured limit, so a regression that makes the limit check silently no-op (e.g., if `s.deviceLimit` were not threaded through) would still pass the test. Add an explicit `CountDevices` assertion between the two `CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup logs use Error level and log nil error on success

Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579 use r.log.Error(...) for routine cleanup progress messages (e.g. 'Annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned tags'). The function already returns early on a non-nil error, so when execution reaches these log statements the err value is always nil, yet it is still passed as the 'err' key. The result is that every successful cleanup cycle emits Error-level log records containing a nil error. Combined with the cleanup ticker being moved to 1 minute in cleanup.go, this means an Error-level log is emitted on every pass of the cleanup job, polluting error monitoring and breaking any alerting/log filters that assume Error level indicates a real failure. The level should be Debug or Info, and the 'err' key should only be logged when non-nil (or moved into the error branch). Existing call sites in the same package use r.log.Info for routine ops (line 410: 'delete') and cleanup.go uses Debug for normal results (line 129), so this is also inconsistent with surrounding code.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup ticker shortened from 10m to 1m without justification

The Run loop's ticker was changed from time.Minute * 10 to time.Minute * 1. This is a 10x increase in cleanup job frequency that is unrelated to the deadlock fix described in the PR (which is in xorm_store.go). The change is not mentioned in the PR description and is bundled with the deadlock fix. With a 9 minute per-job timeout (line 89) and now a 1 minute tick, a slow cleanup cycle (e.g. while there are many annotations to remove) will cause the next tick to fire while clean(ctx) is still executing, leading to overlapping clean() invocations on the same shared parent context. This risk is amplified by the new 'fetchIDs then deleteByIDs' pattern, which performs two DB roundtrips per batch instead of one. The ticker value should either be reverted to 10 minutes or justified/handled separately, and the loop should track whether a clean cycle is in progress to avoid concurrent runs.

false_positives.candidate:
Integration tests now skipped under -short with no unit-level coverage added

TestAnnotationCleanUp and TestOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst were renamed to TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp / TestIntegrationOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst and both gained a testing.Short() skip. These were the only tests that exercised CleanAnnotations / CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags in any way. They required a real DB before too, but now they run in zero CI configurations that use -short, and the deadlock regression that this PR fixes has no unit-test coverage of its own. There should be at least one non-DB unit test that exercises the new helpers (e.g. that untilDoneOrCancelled terminates on ctx.Done() and on zero affected rows, and that deleteByIDs short-circuits on an empty id list), so the new code paths are exercised in short mode and refactoring does not silently break them.

SQL and parameters are passed as separate args to session.Exec

In deleteByIDs, the call is:

    res, err := session.Exec(append([]any{sql}, args...)...)

The first element of the variadic args slice is the statement text and the remaining elements are the bind parameters. xorm's Session.Exec expects (sql string, args ...interface{}); passing the SQL string as a positional argument via the args slice is unusual and depends on undocumented behavior of the dialect's Exec wrapper. Several xorm code paths treat the first element as a parameter and prepend the SQL separately, which can lead to the SQL being interpreted as part of the parameter list (e.g. on PostgreSQL where the driver receives the SQL as a query string only when calling Exec(sql, args...) directly). This should be called as session.Exec(sql, args...) to match the rest of the file (e.g. line 415, 419, 426, 430) and avoid silently malforming the query on some drivers.

cleanupWHERE clause is built from annotationType without an AND before created filter

The condition built for the MaxAge branch is:

    cond := fmt.Sprintf(`%s AND created < %v ORDER BY id DESC %s`, annotationType, cutoffDate, r.db.GetDialect().Limit(...))

The annotationType argument (e.g. 'alert_id > 0 AND dashboard_id > 0' for dashboard annotations, or 'alert_id = 0 AND dashboard_id = 0' for API annotations) is concatenated directly. If any caller passes a type filter that ends with OR rather than AND, the trailing 'AND created <' will silently change the operator precedence. More importantly, the MaxCount branch builds:

    cond := fmt.Sprintf(`%s ORDER BY id DESC %s`, annotationType, r.db.GetDialect().LimitOffset(...))

without any check that annotationType contains a WHERE fragment rather than a full clause. The comment in the code refers to annotationType as 'e.g. alert_id > 0 AND dashboard_id > 0', but the function silently trusts the caller. There is no validation, and an accidental empty string would produce 'SELECT id FROM annotation  ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT N', which would happily walk the entire annotation table per batch (and there is no OFFSET/limit on the SELECT itself other than what the dialect appends). A guard against empty annotationType or a small comment/contract would make this safer.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
DeleteCollection async legacy call recorded as storage duration

In the DeleteCollection async goroutine, the elapsed time of d.Legacy.DeleteCollection is fed to d.recordStorageDuration(...). Every other write path correctly uses recordLegacyDuration for the legacy leg; this one is mislabeled, so DeleteCollection legacy latency will be merged into the unified-storage histogram and the real legacy histogram will not see those calls.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete success path labels metric with name instead of Kind

On successful d.Storage.Delete, d.recordStorageDuration is called with `name` as the kind label, while every other path (and the failing branch on line 103) uses options.Kind. As a result, the storage latency histogram for Delete will be tagged with the resource name instead of the resource kind, breaking grouping with all other operations.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy Create inherits request context that is cancelled when the response returns

The async Create goroutine derives its timeout from the inbound request context: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)`. That ctx is the apiserver request context, which is cancelled as soon as the handler writes the response and returns. The whole purpose of mode 3 is to write to legacy "as a safe measure" after the request returns; here that guarantee is broken, and the legacy write will frequently be aborted by ctx.Done() before completing. Use a detached context (e.g., context.Background()) with the klog logger still attached.

Async legacy Create uses the pre-storage object, not the stored object

After d.Storage.Create succeeds, the returned `created` object contains the UID, resourceVersion, creation timestamp, etc. that unified storage assigned. The async goroutine calls d.Legacy.Create with the original `obj` parameter instead, so the legacy store never sees the metadata assigned by storage (or assigns its own), producing two records with different identities for what should be the same resource. The legacy record is effectively orphaned from the unified one.

Async legacy Delete inherits request context

Same problem as the Create goroutine on line 51: the Delete goroutine derives its context from the request context with WithTimeoutCause(... 10s). The legacy Delete will be cancelled when the apiserver request finishes, so the safety-net legacy delete is not guaranteed to run to completion.

Async legacy DeleteCollection inherits request context

Same as above: the DeleteCollection goroutine derives its context from the request context with WithTimeoutCause(... 10s), so the legacy bulk delete will be cancelled when the handler returns and the two stores will diverge.

Async legacy Update inherits request context

The async Update goroutine derives its context from the request context with WithTimeoutCause(... 10s). The legacy Update will be cancelled when the apiserver request finishes, so the safety-net legacy update is not guaranteed to run. The legacy store can therefore permanently diverge from unified storage on any request that finishes inside 10s.

Async legacy Update re-evaluates UpdatedObjectInfo against legacy's current state

The async Update goroutine passes the original objInfo to d.Legacy.Update. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is called inside the legacy store against whatever it currently holds, not against the state storage just wrote. The previous implementation wrapped objInfo around the resolved object and passed the same wrapped value to both stores so they would apply identical changes; here the legacy store can compute and persist a different version, causing legacy and storage to diverge.

Create records storage failure as legacy duration

In DualWriterMode3.Create, when d.Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recording the storage duration. Because recordLegacyDuration and recordStorageDuration are distinct Prometheus metrics, a storage-side failure will be misattributed to the legacy backend. Anyone alerting or graphing on legacy failures will see storage failures, and storage failures will be invisible. Use recordStorageDuration(true, ...) here.

Mode3 doc comment describes the wrong write order

The comment on newDualWriterMode3 says "Mode 3 represents writing to LegacyStorage and Storage and reading from Storage." The actual behavior implemented below is: write synchronously to Storage, then fire-and-forget an asynchronous write to LegacyStorage, and read only from Storage. The comment therefore misleads readers about both the ordering and the async nature of mode 3.

TestMode3_Create never asserts that the legacy async Create actually ran

TestMode3_Create registers an expectation on the legacy store mock via setupLegacyFn but the goroutine that should satisfy it is never synchronized with (no wait, no channel, no AssertExpectations). The test currently passes even if the legacy async write is removed or short-circuited, so the very behavior mode 3 introduces - the legacy safety-net write - is effectively untested.

TestMode3_DeleteCollection has no legacy setup or assertion at all

The testCase struct does not include setupLegacyFn and no mock expectation is registered for d.Legacy.DeleteCollection. The implementation runs an async legacy DeleteCollection but nothing in this test exercises it - the safety-net behavior on the bulk-delete path is entirely uncovered.

TestMode3_Get does not verify legacy Get is never called

Mode 3 reads must come from storage only, but TestMode3_Get never asserts that the legacy store is not called (the analogous TestMode1_Get uses us.AssertNotCalled on Delete). A future change that accidentally adds a legacy Get would not be caught.

TestMode3_Get uses a local prometheus registry while the rest of the file uses the package-level p

All other tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go and dualwriter_mode1_test.go use the package-level `p`; TestMode3_Get creates its own `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` inside the test body, masking the global and being a leftover from before the global existed. Minor, but should be aligned.

TestMode3_Update never asserts the legacy async Update ran

TestMode3_Update registers a mock expectation for legacy Update but does not synchronize with or assert against the async goroutine. The same problem as Create: the legacy safety-net update is not actually verified.

Update records storage failure as legacy duration

In DualWriterMode3.Update, when d.Storage.Update fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration. Same effect as in Create: a unified-storage Update failure is reported as a legacy failure, silently corrupting the two latency/error time series. Use recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Write lock held during I/O blocks all readers and causes redundant work

The write lock acquired at line 48 is held while performing I/O (readWebAssetsFromFile on line 60 and the disabled readWebAssetsFromCDN on line 56), so every concurrent reader is blocked until that I/O completes. Combined with the double-checked locking pattern (RLock at line 41, then Lock at line 48), multiple goroutines that race to populate the cache after startup will all redundantly execute the file read and overwrite each other's results. The data race itself is correctly fixed, but a more efficient pattern would use sync.Once (with a reset path for Dev mode) or release the lock around the I/O and re-acquire it only to publish the result, so only one goroutine performs the slow work and readers are never blocked by it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:

false_negatives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

false_positives.candidate:
Alternate construction path for SQLCommand is not gated

`NewSQLCommand` and the exported `UnmarshalSQLCommand` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` are still publicly callable and do not consult the `enableSqlExpressions` feature check that was added in `pkg/expr/reader.go`. They rely on `sql.TablesList` failing because the new `DB` stub returns `"not implemented"`, which surfaces as the generic `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", ...)` with the public message `"error reading SQL command"`. This is inconsistent with the more specific `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` produced from the reader path, and it means any caller that bypasses `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` gets a different (and less informative) error. The disablement should be enforced at a single chokepoint (or both paths should return the same clear message) so the security state is consistent regardless of entry point.

Error message misleads users about feature status

The error returned to users is `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This wording is misleading: SQL expressions are implemented (the package exists, the parser, command, and DB stubs are all wired up); the feature has been deliberately disabled as a security mitigation for CVE-2024-9264. A user (or operator) reading this error would conclude the functionality was never built rather than that it is currently turned off for safety. Consider something like `"sqlExpressions are disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264)"` so the situation is clear and operators can grep for the CVE in their dashboards/logs.

No tests for the security mitigation

The PR is a security fix that disables the entire SQL Expressions feature, replacing the `go-duck` backend with stubs and adding a feature-gated branch in `ReadQuery`. There are no new tests verifying:
- that `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` now returns the expected error,
- that `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` methods all return `"not implemented"`,
- that `NewSQLCommand` / `UnmarshalSQLCommand` no longer succeed.

For a CVE-driven fix, regression tests pinning the disabled behaviour are essential so that a future re-enable cannot accidentally land without an explicit test change.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BuildIndex loses per-key serialization, allowing same-key races

The diff removes `b.cacheMu.Lock(); defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()` from the top of `BuildIndex` and only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. Previously, two concurrent calls to `BuildIndex` for the same `key` were serialized, so `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` (lines ~96-102) was only ever invoked once per directory. With the new finer-grained locking, two callers that race through `getOrCreateIndex` for the same key when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold` will both call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory. bleve's New on an already-existing directory either errors or reopens stale state; one call returns an error to a caller even though the index they wanted was successfully created and is sitting in the cache. `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` already has a TODO admitting it has no per-key mutex, so this relaxation of the backend's serialization makes a known race easier to trigger. Consider keeping the exclusive lock around the directory creation (or adding a per-key `sync.Map` / singleflight) and only using the finer-grained lock to protect the cache map mutation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu

`bleveBackend.TotalDocs` does `for _, v := range b.cache { ... }` with no read-lock on `cacheMu`, while `BuildIndex` writes `b.cache[key] = idx` under `cacheMu`. Go map iteration concurrent with writes panics with "concurrent map iteration and map write". The new `s.log.Info(..., "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` added in `search.go` happens after `group.Wait()` so it is safe today, but `TotalDocs` is part of the `SearchBackend` interface and any future caller (e.g., a metrics endpoint, health check, or test) that invokes it while index construction is in flight will crash the process. Either take `cacheMu.RLock()` for the iteration, or iterate a snapshot of the keys under the lock.

false_positives.candidate:
Eager Init swallows cancelation from the caller's context

`NewResourceServer` now passes its locally constructed `ctx` (a `context.WithCancel(context.Background(), ...)` wrapping a static service-account identity) into `s.Init(ctx)`. Inside `Init`, this `ctx` is forwarded to `search.init(ctx)`, which in turn calls `s.storage.GetResourceStats(ctx, ...)` and `s.storage.ListIterator(ctx, ...)` for every namespace being indexed. Those calls now use a context that lives for the lifetime of the server and is only cancelled when `s.Stop` runs — they never see a deadline or the caller's cancellation. That is fine for a production server, but `NewResourceServer` is also called from `InitializeModuleServer` in tests and from any tooling that builds a transient server. The previous per-handler `s.Init(ctx)` propagated the per-request deadline/cancellation, so a hung DB could be aborted by closing the test context. With the eager call, an unresponsive backend during index build will block `NewResourceServer` indefinitely, which in turn blocks module startup with no way to cancel it from outside.

Postgres integration test now silently skipped with a TODO

The diff adds `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip(...) }` to the only integration test that exercises the storage server target with a real DB. Combined with the existing `sqlite3` skip, the test is now skipped for every DB type the CI matrix runs against — it provides no coverage. The TODO comment admits the test "works locally" but not in Drone, strongly suggesting the new eager `Init()` in `NewResourceServer` exposes an init-only failure mode that the lazy initialization hid. A `t.Skip` is the wrong fix here: the test should be made to pass for both `Init()` orderings, or split so that the storage-server integration is verified separately for postgres. Otherwise a regression in the eager-init path on postgres will land unnoticed.

Two long-running WatchWriteEvents pollers run for the same backend

After this change, both `searchSupport.init` (lines ~202-213 in search.go) and `server.initWatcher` (line 752) each call `s.backend.WatchWriteEvents(...)`, which for the SQL backend (`pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:558`) starts its own 100 ms poller goroutine. The `errgroup` already sets the search index up; now the broadcaster independently starts a second poller querying the same resource history tables. Two pollers every 100 ms doubles DB load, doubles history scans, and produces two independent `mostRecentRV` writers and two event streams. The order swap (initWatcher first vs. search.init first) does not change this — both sequences still leave the search support's watcher running alongside `initWatcher`. The author's stated goal was just to parallelize index build across distinct keys; the duplicate watcher is unrelated and should be removed (let the search support's handler pipe into the broadcaster, or use the broadcaster as the single event source).

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Broken IDP cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin causes test pollution

In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` test, every `create` call is followed by `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`. The literal string `"alias"` is not an alias of any IDP created by this test (the aliases are `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19` and `idp-alias-20`), so when the cleanup runs, `get("alias")` returns `null` and `null::remove` throws a NullPointerException. None of the 21 IDPs created by this test are actually removed, so they leak into subsequent tests (and into the IDP alias cache of the test realm), which can break other organization cache tests. The same pattern is repeated in the new test on lines 381 and 425. The alias variable should be used (e.g. `idpRep.getAlias()` or a captured `final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

false_positives.candidate:
REALM_ONLY cache searchKey includes organizationId unnecessarily

In `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)`, the searchKey is computed as `organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""`. However, the underlying JPA implementation explicitly sets `ORGANIZATION_ID=null` in its search options for `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` (and never consults the input `organizationId` in that branch), so the result is identical regardless of the supplied `organizationId`. By baking `organizationId` into the searchKey, callers that legitimately pass non-null values for `REALM_ONLY` (the Javadoc explicitly says `organizationId` is ignored when `mode` is `REALM_ONLY`) get a fresh, separate `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry every time, defeating the cache for any caller that does not happen to pass `null`. The searchKey should be fixed to a constant (e.g. always "") for `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` so all REALM_ONLY lookups share one cache entry.

getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without null check

The newly added clause `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` assumes `idp.getConfig()` is never null. The `IdentityProviderModel` `config` field is mutable and can be set to `null`; `getConfig()` does not lazily initialize it in all versions, and callers using the SPI (e.g. test code, custom providers, internal `update()` flows that operate on partially populated models) may produce a model with a null `config` map, causing an NPE here. Because this predicate is invoked from `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`/`registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` on every IDP `create`/`update`/`remove`, a single such model will crash the whole IDP write path. Either guard `getConfig()` against null (e.g. `idp.getConfig() != null && Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`) or normalize the field in the model.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JCE default provider, not BouncyCastle

`getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`. This returns whatever JCE provider supplies the default keystore type on the host JVM (typically SUN/SunPKCS11/SunJSSE), not BouncyCastle. Callers that explicitly rely on a BC provider (e.g. to ask BC for algorithms/curves not present in the SUN provider) will silently get the SUN provider instead and may fail with `NoSuchAlgorithmException` later. Either return an actual BouncyCastleProvider (as `DefaultCryptoProvider` does) or, if BC is intentionally not bundled in the authz-client, throw UnsupportedOperationException so the failure mode is obvious.

true_positives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead code: discarded ASN1Encoder writes in concatenatedRSToASN1DER

In the anonymous ECDSACryptoProvider implementation, the two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` (lines 114-115) create new ASN1Encoder instances, write a full INTEGER TLV into their internal ByteArrayOutputStream, and then discard the result. The actual DER sequence is built immediately after by the four chained `ASN1Encoder.create().write(...)` calls inside `writeDerSeq`. The discarded writes are wasted allocations and I/O and should be deleted to avoid misleading readers into thinking they are part of the encoding.

true_positives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
readSequence silently returns empty list for indefinite-length sequences and does not check for end-of-contents

`readSequence` reads a length and then loops `while (length > 0)`. When `readLength()` returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (length byte `0x80`), the loop never executes and the method returns an empty `ArrayList`. The caller in `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS` then fails with the misleading error "Invalid sequence with size different to 2". While DER (X.690 §10.1) forbids indefinite lengths for sequences, accepting BER signatures that use them would require consuming elements until the end-of-contents octets `0x00 0x00`. As written, any non-DER BER-encoded signature coming from another library will produce a confusing error rather than a clear one.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

false_positives.candidate:
Duplicate junit and hamcrest test dependencies

The diff adds junit and hamcrest test dependencies at lines 61-71, but these dependencies already exist earlier in the file (visible in the full content at the same coordinates). Maven allows duplicate dependency declarations but it is a defect: it produces a confusing POM, may trigger Maven warnings on some versions, and makes future maintenance error-prone (e.g., changing scope in one place but not the other). The added junit/hamcrest block should be removed since the dependencies are already declared.

Most CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException; authz-client standalone usage is broken

`AuthzClientCryptoProvider` is registered as the SPI provider for `org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` in `authz/client/src/main/resources/META-INF/services/...`. However, nearly every method on the interface (`getAlgorithmProvider`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getOCSPProver`, `getIdentityExtractorProvider`, `getEcdsaCryptoProvider().getPublicFromPrivate`, `createECParams`, `getKeyPairGen`, `getKeyFactory`, `getAesCbcCipher`, `getAesGcmCipher`, `getSecretKeyFact`, `getX509CertFactory`, `getCertStore`, `getCertPathBuilder`, `getSignature`, `wrapFactoryForTruststore`) is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. The authz-client uses these facilities (notably `getSignature`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getKeyPairGen`/`getKeyFactory`) when authenticating with signed-JWT client credentials and when parsing keys/certificates. When this module is used standalone (the documented intent), any such operation will throw UnsupportedOperationException at runtime, breaking client credential flows that involve private-key JWT, mutual TLS, or PEM key material. The PR should either implement these methods or document explicitly that the authz-client only supports the subset used for ECDSA R/S <-> DER conversion and fail fast at init time otherwise.

Test only covers DER -> concat -> DER -> concat, not the inverse and not the values themselves

The `test(ECDSAAlgorithm)` helper signs data with the JCE provider (DER output), converts to concatenated R/S, then back to DER and back to R/S, asserting the two concatenated forms are equal. It never verifies (a) the direct concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip with a known concatenated input, (b) that the produced DER bytes decode to the same BigInteger r,s values produced by the JCE Signature, and (c) that the produced concatenated bytes, when fed back into `Signature.verify` via `Signature.getInstance("NONEwithECDSA")` with the same algorithm, actually verify. Without (c) the test cannot catch sign-magnitude vs. two's-complement bugs, leading-zero handling bugs, or off-by-one in the `arraySize = len + 1` shift (which always prepends a 0 byte and can produce non-minimal DER).

logger.debugf called with a non-format string, will throw on class names containing %

`logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-built string as the format argument. JBoss Logger's `debugf(String, Object...)` interprets the first argument as a `printf`-style format and expects additional varargs matching any `%` specifiers. If any class name returned by `ServiceLoader` contains a `%` (legal in JVM class names), `MissingFormatArgumentException` or similar will be thrown every time more than one provider is found, surfacing as an unexpected stack trace at debug level and, depending on JUL/LogManager configuration, potentially being promoted to a higher level. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` or `logger.debugf("%s", builder.toString())` instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Listener gated by V1 feature flag disables cleanup in V2

The new `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` wraps the entire event body, so when only the V2 feature (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`) is enabled the `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent` and `GroupRemovedEvent` handlers are skipped entirely. Previously the handlers ran unconditionally, and `MgmtPermissionsV2.roles()` still has a real `setPermissionsEnabled` implementation that is no longer invoked, so role/group permission state will be left orphaned when those entities are removed in a V2-only realm. The check should be `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ || ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, or the per-handler calls must selectively skip the V2-unsupported `ClientPermissions.setPermissionsEnabled`.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getClientsWithPermission returns the literal string "Clients" as a client id

`getClientsWithPermission` iterates every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes the schema's "all-clients" resource (created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` with name="Clients" and type="Clients"). If the all-clients resource has the requested scope granted, `hasGrantedPermission` returns true and the string `"Clients"` is added to the returned set. The contract of the method is a set of client ids; returning `"Clients"` causes callers (e.g. code that filters `realm.clients().get(...)`) to either crash trying to look up a client with that id or silently behave as if no clients matched. The handler must skip the resource whose name equals `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (and, when that resource is granted, return the set of all client ids in the realm, not the literal "Clients").

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Potential NPE when all-clients resource does not exist

In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is null the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That method returns null when admin permissions are disabled, when the type is unknown, or when the resource was never created. The next line then calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource, which will NPE inside the policy store. The fallback path must null-check the result of `getResourceTypeResource` and return `false` when null.

true_positives.golden_comment: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unused method and dead imports

`getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is defined but never referenced from anywhere in the class. The accompanying imports (`ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AccessToken`) and the `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` static import are also dead. The unused `logger` field is declared on line 51 as well. This is dead code introduced together with the new class and should be removed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

false_positives.candidate:
No test exercises canMapClientScopeRoles, canManageClientScopes or canView(ClientScopeModel)

ClientPermissionsV2 implements `canMapClientScopeRoles` (backed by `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`), `canManageClientScopes` (backed by the `MANAGE` scope) and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` (backed by `VIEW`/`MANAGE`), but PermissionClientTest only covers `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`, `VIEW`, `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`. The `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope is registered in the schema but is not exercised by any test, leaving the new authorization logic uncovered. A test mirroring `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` should grant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and verify that client-scope role mappings can and cannot be performed.

getResourceName has no case for the Clients resource type

`getResourceName` special-cases the `USERS` resource type (translating the all-users marker to "All users" and otherwise looking up the user to return the username). For the new `CLIENTS` resource type the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, so client-typed resources will be displayed as the client UUID (the stored name) instead of a friendly label, and the all-clients resource will appear as the literal string "Clients" rather than "All clients". A symmetric branch for `CLIENTS.getType()` should be added.

testManageOnlyOneClient assumes at least 2 default client scopes

After granting `MANAGE`, the test does `ClientScopeRepresentation clientScopeRep = defaultClientScopes.get(1);` (and again on line 174). If the realm configuration registers fewer than two default client scopes for `myclient` (the realm-admin permissions config in this PR adds new scopes that are stored on the admin-permissions client, not on the application client), `get(1)` throws IndexOutOfBoundsException and the test fails for reasons unrelated to the authorization logic. The test should either assert `defaultClientScopes.size() >= 2` or iterate by content rather than by hard-coded index.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
picocli.exit() will not compile

The new code calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`, but the only picocli import in this file is `import picocli.CommandLine;`. `picocli` is a package, not a class, so there is no static `exit(int)` method to call and the expression does not resolve to anything. The code will fail to compile. The author most likely intended `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`, or to delegate back to the picocli CommandLine via `getCommandLine().get().setExecutionResult(...)` / throwing a `CommandLine.ParameterException`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3

The constant `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from `4` to `3`, and `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` now occupies the old slot. Any automation (CI/CD scripts, GitOps pipelines) that was already treating exit code `4` as "recreate upgrade required" will silently misclassify that condition as "feature disabled" after this change. Even though the surrounding tool is preview, the documentation still presents the exit codes as a stable contract for automation and the change is undocumented in the diff. The new value `3` also collides conceptually with the standard "recreate / must shut down" message, which is fine semantically, yet the previous mapping was different. At minimum this should be called out as a breaking change to the preview contract, and ideally the doc in update-compatibility.adoc should explicitly note that exit code `4` previously meant recreate and now means feature disabled.

false_positives.candidate:
picocli.exit() will not compile

Same defect as in UpdateCompatibilityCheck: `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` is invoked, but the imports contain only `import picocli.CommandLine;`. `picocli` is a package name; there is no class named `picocli` with a static `exit` method to resolve. The new feature-disabled branch will not compile. Use `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` or the appropriate picocli mechanism (e.g. setting the CommandLine execution result).

testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts message, not exit code 4

The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` test verifies the user-facing error string but does not assert the exit code. The whole point of the new `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` constant and the matching doc table entry for exit code 4 is to give automation a reliable signal. The test should also `assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode())` (or the framework equivalent) so that a future regression where the command prints the message but returns a different exit code is caught.

updatecompatibility macro hardcodes --features=rolling-updates

The `updatecompatibility` macro now unconditionally appends ` --features=rolling-updates` to every rendered example, including usage that is meant to demonstrate the "feature not enabled" case (the very behavior asserted by `testFeatureNotEnabled`). Any documentation page that uses this macro will show users an example that explicitly turns the feature on, which makes it impossible to demonstrate the off-by-default behavior in docs. The macro should at most render the flag conditionally, or pages needing the negative example should be able to opt out.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
V2 canManage() grants group-management privileges to VIEW-only admins

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-argument) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, so an admin who only has the `view` scope on the 'Groups' all-resource is treated as if they can manage groups. This affects every admin endpoint guarded by `auth.groups().requireManage()` without a specific group argument, in particular GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups) and the manage-only branches of GroupResource (updateGroup, deleteGroup, addChild, role-mappings). A user policy that grants only `view` on the `Groups` resource type now lets the holder create, rename, delete and reassign top-level groups, violating least privilege. The interface javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() even codifies this behavior. V1's canManage() correctly limits itself to the `manage-users` admin role; the V2 override should match that and check only `MANAGE` (or equivalently delegate to a per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` over an all-groups resource).

true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource.getId() instead of resource.getName()

Inside `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the iteration is `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> { hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...); granted.add(groupResource.getId()); })`. In the V2 schema, per-group resources are created with `name == groupId` (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup / getOrCreateResource), so `groupResource.getId()` is the resource's own auto-generated UUID, not the group's id. Two concrete consequences: (a) `hasPermission` calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` which never matches the per-group resource, so every per-group permission check falls back to the all-groups evaluation and ignores scope restrictions on the specific group; (b) the returned set is populated with resource UUIDs that the user search interprets as group ids (see UsersResource.searchForUser where the set is set as `UserModel.GROUPS`), so the user filter ends up matching no real groups and the entire view-by-group filter is broken. Both `getId()` calls should be `getName()` to mirror the V1 implementation that used `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`.

false_positives.candidate:
Missing test that VIEW on Groups does not imply manage privileges

GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest grants a `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type in `testViewGroups` but only exercises the list endpoint. There is no test that asserts a VIEW-only admin cannot create, update, delete groups or add child groups. Given the canManage() privilege escalation introduced in GroupPermissionsV2 (see security finding), a regression test should be added that grants only VIEW scope and expects 403 on POST /groups, PUT /groups/{id}, DELETE /groups/{id}, and POST /groups/{id}/children. Without it the escalation can re-recur unnoticed.

NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null

In `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, when no per-group resource is found, the code does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` followed immediately by `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can legitimately return null (it returns null whenever `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, when the resourceType argument is null, when the schema type is unknown, or when the 'Groups' resource has not yet been persisted in the resource store). Passing that null into `findByResource(server, null)` will NPE, crashing the admin REST call. Guard the lookup with a null check, mirroring the equivalent code in UserPermissionsV2 which has the same defect.

NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null

`hasPermission(UserModel user, ...)` performs the same fallback as GroupPermissionsV2: `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE); if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`. When `getResourceTypeResource` returns null (feature disabled, schema not yet initialized, or 'Users' resource missing), `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` throws a NullPointerException. This affects every V2 canView/canManage/canImpersonate/canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership call path. Add a null guard before `findByResource`.

Removed AdminRoles.ADMIN fallback may deny master-realm admins under FGAP V2

The pre-existing V2 overrides for canView(UserModel), canManage(UserModel), canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership used to short-circuit on `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, ...)`. The new versions drop the `AdminRoles.ADMIN` role entirely. With AdminPermissionsEnabled + ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 on a child realm, a master-realm administrator holding only the `admin` role (no `manage-users`/`view-users` client role) will no longer satisfy the role check, and only the Authz policy engine will be consulted. Unless the realm admin has explicitly created a UserPolicy mapping the admin user to the 'Users' resource, every user-management call will fail with 403. This is a behavioral regression relative to V1 and the previous V2 implementation; either keep the ADMIN check or document/guarantee that ADMIN implies these scopes via policy.

canManage() javadoc misrepresents required scopes

The javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` says "Or if it has a permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` or `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` groups". That text legitimizes the privilege-escalation behavior implemented in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (a viewer should not be a manager). The doc should match V1 semantics: only `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` (or the `manage-users` admin role) grants manage; `view` should not.

true_positives.golden_comment: The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
replaceFirst only removes the first occurrence of a repeated anchor

`value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` only replaces the FIRST match in `value`, not all matches. If a translation legitimately reuses the same anchor tag more than once and the English source only has one occurrence, only the first occurrence is stripped; the remaining occurrences are then passed to the OWASP sanitizer, which (with `POLICY_SOME_HTML` not allowing `<a>`) will escape them and produce a spurious "Illegal HTML" error. Combined with the stale-Matcher issue above, the second `<a href="X">` is also reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Use `replaceAll`, or iterate via the matcher and reconstruct the string, to handle repeated anchors correctly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.
The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').
Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

false_positives.candidate:
Breaking change to i18next escape syntax in JS-side resource bundle

The value of `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The double-brace form `{{0}}` / `{{1}}` / `{{2}}` is i18next's escape syntax for producing literal `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` text, which is what account-ui uses. After this change, i18next will interpret `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the `{2,choice,...}` clause as placeholders / interpolation tokens. i18next does not implement Java MessageFormat choice format, and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is not valid i18next interpolation syntax, so the message will either fail to interpolate or be displayed verbatim with broken `{...}` text instead of the localized error. The previous value (`value(s)`) was a deliberate, working i18next-compatible rendering of the message; this PR regresses that. The new format belongs only on the Java side (e.g. `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties`), where it does belong.

Comment mischaracterises '<1>' as a "numeric tag"

The comment states the sanitizer escapes 'numeric tags like `<1>`'. There is no concept of a numeric tag in HTML or in the OWASP sanitizer; the sanitizer simply treats the literal text `<1>` as an invalid HTML tag (because tag names must start with a letter per the policy) and escapes the '<' and '>' characters. `<1>` here is an i18next / React-Intl style indexed placeholder, not a numeric tag. The wording will mislead future maintainers about what the sanitizer is doing and why `<1>` survives the round-trip via `unescapeHtml4`.

File is read and parsed twice per verification

`verify()` reads the file with `Files.readString(file.toPath())` for duplicate-key detection, and then `verifySafeHtml()` opens another `FileInputStream` and parses the same file as `PropertyResourceBundle`. The two reads produce no consistency guarantee (a file could change between reads) and double the I/O. Either parse once into a `PropertyResourceBundle` and reuse it for both checks, or read the bytes once and wrap them in two parsers. Not a correctness bug, but the verifier runs over hundreds of message bundles during a theme build, so the duplication is non-trivial.

No positive test that valid HTML in a translation is accepted The four new tests only assert that illegal HTML is detected (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`) and that duplicates are detected. There is no positive test that exercises the happy path of `verifySafeHtml`: e.g. an English value containing `bar` and a translation containing `bar` (or `bar`) that should NOT be reported. Without it, a regression in the sanitizer flow (e.g. always escaping ``) would not be caught by the test suite. Add a test resource pair (`allowedHtml_en.properties` + `allowedHtml_de.properties`) with matching allowed tags and assert that the message list does not contain "Illegal HTML".

No test for the `{2,choice,...}` normalization of `error-invalid-multivalued-size`

`normalizeValue` strips `{N,choice,...}` clauses for `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` specifically. This special case is central to the PR because that key was just rewritten across every bundle to use this Java MessageFormat choice syntax. There is no test fixture nor assertion that (a) a translation whose choice clause differs from the English (e.g. different `1#value|1<values` text) is still accepted, and (b) a translation with literal `<` outside a choice clause is rejected. The whole point of this PR is to make `error-invalid-multivalued-size` valid, but the only protection against regressing it is the production code itself, with no regression test in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest`.

Regex character class too broad due to '-' being treated as range operator

The regex `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` contains the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`. In Java regex, the dash '-' that is not at the start or end of the class and not escaped is interpreted as a range operator. With the previous 'A-Z' range ending at 'Z' (0x5A), the '-_' is parsed as a range from 'Z' (0x5A) to '_' (0x5F), which silently adds '[', '\', ']', '^', and '_' to the matched character set. The author clearly intended `[a-zA-Z_]` (or `[a-zA-Z_-]` with '-' placed last so it is a literal). For typical locale codes (letters + underscore) this happens to work, but the regex is incorrect and could match unintended characters in path components containing '[', '\', etc. Fix by writing `[a-zA-Z_-]` (dash at the end of the class, making it literal) or `[a-zA-Z_]`.

Same i18next breaking change in admin-ui resource bundle

Same regression as in the account-ui bundle: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,...}`). The admin-ui is also a React/i18next app, so the change replaces working placeholder-escaping with placeholders that i18next will try to interpolate, and embeds a Java MessageFormat choice clause (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`) that i18next does not understand. Result at runtime: malformed interpolation and/or broken/untranslated text shown to the admin user.

Trailing newline stripped from `error-invalid-multivalued-size`

The unified diff shows the file ends with `\ No newline at end of file` after this change (the `-` line also had `\ No newline at end of file`). Many editors, linters, and POSIX text tools require files to end with a newline, and several Keycloak bundles historically did so. The fact that the previous version ended without a newline was already a minor smell, but the change also touches a line at the end of the file without restoring the newline. This will show up as a noisy diff in future PRs and may violate any project policy on POSIX file endings.

`public static final String GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE;` resolves to the literal string `"grant_type"`, which is a key name used as a `ClientSessionContext` attribute key, not a grant-type value. The name suggests a grant type such as `authorization_code`. Either the constant should be renamed to make clear it is a session-context attribute key (e.g. `CLIENT_SESSION_CTX_GRANT_TYPE`) or the Javadoc should explain it is the OAuth2 parameter/attribute name, not a grant type value, to avoid misuse such as `ctx.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.AUTHORIZATION_CODE)` style calls.

Both `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` do a non-atomic check-then-put into the `ConcurrentHashMap`s. Two threads can simultaneously take the `null` branch and both write. More importantly, nothing prevents a new grant factory from registering with a shortcut that collides with an existing one after `postInit`, which silently overwrites the existing entry in `grantsByShortcuts` and corrupts lookups in both directions; the startup-only size check in `postInit` does not protect against this hot path.

The encoded prefix has layout [session 0-1][token 2-3][grant 4-5], so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5. Combined with the inverted logic, the matcher never actually verifies the grant type and accepts any 6-char prefix as long as the UUID part is valid.

The previous public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted by this PR. The PR description does not call out this removal, and there is no replacement, so this is an undocumented SPI breaking change.

In `isValid()` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, the implementation returns true as soon as the input matches any raw key in `myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData()` but never mutates the stored credential to remove or flag the consumed code. Because `isValid()` does not track per-code consumption, the `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built by `getCredentials()` from the stored raw `credentialData` will always have `allCodesUsed() == false`. `updateCredential` saves the JSON produced by `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` (which serializes the raw codes) straight into `credentialData` without hashing. The local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` hashes the codes before storage (it relies on `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode` with `NOM_ALGORITHM_TO_HASH`). Storing raw codes in `credentialData` diverges from that posture, so any path that exposes `credentialData` (DB dumps, debug logging, serialized credential model) leaks the user's recovery codes in plaintext. The model reconstructed by `getCredentials()` will also carry these raw codes through `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`, so callers that read `RecoveryCode.getValue()` get the cleartext code.

Test does not verify single-use semantics or credential cleanup

`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only exercises a single successful entry of one recovery code. As a result, an NPE thrown by the reader thread can land in `caughtExceptions` only after the assertion has already passed (or, conversely, the test can pass simply because the timing race was lost on this run). The thread should be joined, and `deletedAll` should be set after the join is set up so the reader can observe the latch, not the main thread.

Even after the null-guard, `if (isUpdated()) return updated.getSubGroupsCount();` is reached only after isUpdated() itself. isUpdated() (lines 70-76) calls `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(...)` and throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")` when `invalidated` is true but the group has been deleted. If the goal of the fix is to make concurrent delete+read not throw, the null-guard should be at the top of the method (e.g., `GroupModel m = getGroupModel(); if (m == null) return null;`) and isUpdated()'s IllegalStateException should be downgraded or guarded, otherwise callers may continue to see exceptions and the test (which catches `Exception`) might still observe a failure via the related IllegalStateException rather than via the originally reported NPE.

false_positives.candidate:
Dead helper `_create_process_for_shard` is never called

The method `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(shard)` (lines 127-132) is defined but has no callers. The only restart path is in `_ensure_processes_alive`, which invokes `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. The single-shard helper is dead code and should either be removed or wired into the restart path so callers can target a specific shard.

Docstring claims one process per shard, but processes shard subsets

The class docstring (line 32) says 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.' That is no longer true: `__init__` actually creates `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes and groups shards via `i % num_processes`. With `flusher_processes=2` and 4 shards, the docstring is misleading and the round-robin assignment also has performance implications (e.g., adjacent shards can end up in different processes and cross shard/processes). The docstring should describe the actual grouping behavior.

CLI help for `--flusher-processes` is misleading

`help="Maximum number of processes for the span flusher. Defaults to 1."` implies that passing e.g. `--flusher-processes 8` always gives 8 processes. In reality `SpanFlusher.__init__` clamps via `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, and the help also describes the CLI default of 1 rather than the SpanFlusher default of `len(assigned_shards)`. If a user passes a value greater than the number of assigned partitions, they will silently get fewer processes than expected. The help should note the cap.

`flusher_processes=0` is silently coerced to `len(assigned_shards)`

In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats 0 as falsy and falls back to one process per shard. An operator passing `--flusher-processes 0` likely expects 'no flusher' or an error, not a default-override that spawns more processes than they asked for. Use an explicit `None` check instead of `or`, or document/validate that 0 is not accepted.

`test_flusher_processes_limit` never submits a message

The new test only asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.max_processes == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2` and that 4 shards are present in `process_to_shards_map`. It does not submit a payload, does not advance drift, and does not assert that any segment reaches the `produce_to_pipe`. The whole point of the multiprocess refactor is that shards split across processes are still flushed end-to-end; this test will silently pass even if the new `_create_process_for_shards` does not correctly wire shards to buffers or if the threading path is broken. Add at least one submit + flush assertion that exercises the cross-process flusher wiring.

`if not process:` guard in `_ensure_processes_alive` is dead

`self.processes` is populated in `_create_process_for_shards` and never has `None` values, so `if not process: continue` (line 222) is unreachable. Either remove the check or, if the intent was to skip dead slots, document why None entries would ever appear (e.g., a future graceful-shutdown slot).

Per-submit Redis memory probe now scales with process count

Original code did one `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call per submit. New code iterates `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`, so the consumer issues N Redis probes per submit where N equals the number of flusher processes (up to one per shard). Even though `submit` is described as not hot, on every call we now do N network round-trips to gather data that conceptually represents the same underlying Redis memory. Consider caching or aggregating memory info once per flush cycle instead of once per submit.

`process.kill()` followed by immediate respawn can produce duplicate flushes

In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the unhealthy process is `kill()`-ed (non-blocking) and `_create_process_for_shards` is invoked immediately. The old subprocess may still be alive for some time (kill delivery, Redis I/O in flight), during which both the old and new flusher processes can independently call `buffer.flush_segments` and `producer.produce` on the same shard. That can produce duplicate `BUFFERED_SEGMENTS` messages on Kafka. The original code had a similar race but only one flusher existed; now that shards are shared across processes, the blast radius is wider. Consider `process.join(timeout)` before respawn, or use `terminate()` plus a join so the previous process truly exits first.

`process_restarts` threshold allows one more restart than the constant suggests

The check is `if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`, followed by increment + respawn. Tracing the counter: it starts at 0, is checked then incremented. With `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS = 10` the counter reaches 11 before `11 > 10` triggers, so the consumer actually restarts the process 11 times before raising, not 10. This is an off-by-one that pre-dates this PR, but it is worth aligning either the constant (to `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS - 1`) or the comparison (`>= MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`) so the cap matches the name.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

Passing that null into `findByResource(server, null)` will NPE, crashing the admin REST call. NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null

`hasPermission(UserModel user, ...)` performs the same fallback as GroupPermissionsV2: `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE); if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`. true_positives.matched_candidate:
replaceFirst only removes the first occurrence of a repeated anchor

`value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` only replaces the FIRST match in `value`, not all matches. If a translation legitimately reuses the same anchor tag more than once and the English source only has one occurrence, only the first occurrence is stripped; the remaining occurrences are then passed to the OWASP sanitizer, which (with `POLICY_SOME_HTML` not allowing `<a>`) will escape them and produce a spurious "Illegal HTML" error. Combined with the stale-Matcher issue above, the second `<a href="X">` is also reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Note that the candidate explicitly references 'the stale-Matcher issue above' and describes the exact scenario of translated text having more anchors than the English source.

false_positives.candidate:
Regex character class too broad due to '-' being treated as range operator

The regex `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` contains the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`. In Java regex, the dash '-' that is not at the start or end of the class and not escaped is interpreted as a range operator. With the previous 'A-Z' range ending at 'Z' (0x5A), the '-_' is parsed as a range from 'Z' (0x5A) to '_' (0x5F), which silently adds '[', '\', ']', '^', and '_' to the matched character set. The author clearly intended `[a-zA-Z_]` (or `[a-zA-Z_-]` with '-' placed last so it is a literal). For typical locale codes (letters + underscore) this happens to work, but the regex is incorrect and could match unintended characters in path components containing '[', '\', etc. Fix by writing `[a-zA-Z_-]` (dash at the end of the class, making it literal) or `[a-zA-Z_]`.

Comment mischaracterises '<1>' as a "numeric tag"

The comment states the sanitizer escapes 'numeric tags like `<1>`'. There is no concept of a numeric tag in HTML or in the OWASP sanitizer; the sanitizer simply treats the literal text `<1>` as an invalid HTML tag (because tag names must start with a letter per the policy) and escapes the '<' and '>' characters. `<1>` here is an i18next / React-Intl style indexed placeholder, not a numeric tag. The wording will mislead future maintainers about what the sanitizer is doing and why `<1>` survives the round-trip via `unescapeHtml4`.

Breaking change to i18next escape syntax in JS-side resource bundle

The value of `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The double-brace form `{{0}}` / `{{1}}` / `{{2}}` is i18next's escape syntax for producing literal `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` text, which is what account-ui uses. After this change, i18next will interpret `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the `{2,choice,...}` clause as placeholders / interpolation tokens. i18next does not implement Java MessageFormat choice format, and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is not valid i18next interpolation syntax, so the message will either fail to interpolate or be displayed verbatim with broken `{...}` text instead of the localized error. The previous value (`value(s)`) was a deliberate, working i18next-compatible rendering of the message; this PR regresses that. The new format belongs only on the Java side (e.g. `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties`), where it does belong.

Same i18next breaking change in admin-ui resource bundle

Same regression as in the account-ui bundle: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,...}`). The admin-ui is also a React/i18next app, so the change replaces working placeholder-escaping with placeholders that i18next will try to interpolate, and embeds a Java MessageFormat choice clause (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`) that i18next does not understand. Result at runtime: malformed interpolation and/or broken/untranslated text shown to the admin user.

No positive test that valid HTML in a translation is accepted The four new tests only assert that illegal HTML is detected (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`) and that duplicates are detected. There is no positive test that exercises the happy path of `verifySafeHtml`: e.g. an English value containing `bar` and a translation containing `bar` (or `bar`) that should NOT be reported. Without it, a regression in the sanitizer flow (e.g. always escaping ``) would not be caught by the test suite. Add a test resource pair (`allowedHtml_en.properties` + `allowedHtml_de.properties`) with matching allowed tags and assert that the message list does not contain "Illegal HTML".

No test for the `{2,choice,...}` normalization of `error-invalid-multivalued-size`

`normalizeValue` strips `{N,choice,...}` clauses for `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` specifically. This special case is central to the PR because that key was just rewritten across every bundle to use this Java MessageFormat choice syntax. There is no test fixture nor assertion that (a) a translation whose choice clause differs from the English (e.g. different `1#value|1<values` text) is still accepted, and (b) a translation with literal `<` outside a choice clause is rejected. The whole point of this PR is to make `error-invalid-multivalued-size` valid, but the only protection against regressing it is the production code itself, with no regression test in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest`.

File is read and parsed twice per verification

`verify()` reads the file with `Files.readString(file.toPath())` for duplicate-key detection, and then `verifySafeHtml()` opens another `FileInputStream` and parses the same file as `PropertyResourceBundle`. The two reads produce no consistency guarantee (a file could change between reads) and double the I/O. Either parse once into a `PropertyResourceBundle` and reuse it for both checks, or read the bytes once and wrap them in two parsers. Not a correctness bug, but the verifier runs over hundreds of message bundles during a theme build, so the duplication is non-trivial.

Trailing newline stripped from `error-invalid-multivalued-size`

The unified diff shows the file ends with `\ No newline at end of file` after this change (the `-` line also had `\ No newline at end of file`). Many editors, linters, and POSIX text tools require files to end with a newline, and several Keycloak bundles historically did so. The fact that the previous version ended without a newline was already a minor smell, but the change also touches a line at the end of the file without restoring the newline. This will show up as a noisy diff in future PRs and may violate any project policy on POSIX file endings.
